recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-13353 unless the work group wants new guidance beyond the published resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-13353 was a Published FHIR-core datatypes change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking for clearer guidance on how to constrain units on Quantity. The accepted resolution was to update the Quantity datatype to reference the terminologies page that describes constraining units used in Quantity.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites svn revision 14154. In git history this is 07b20b4fc864ed477db0166f80391ea75878aada, which added Quantity text saying the context of use may require a code from a particular system or a value set and linked to Using Terminologies for binding Quantity to a value set to constrain unit codes.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini marks Quantity as a current normative datatype with can-bind and has-units characteristics. Current source/datatypes.html still contains the FHIR-13353 Quantity link, and source/terminologies.html explicitly summarizes Quantity binding in terms of Quantity.code and Quantity.system. The original Zulip thread confirms the ambiguity was among allowedUnits, direct Quantity.code/system binding, and value-set binding. Later FHIR-20394 and FHIR-37363 clarify questionnaire-specific unitOption/unitValueSet behavior but do not supersede the general Quantity datatype guidance. The old elementdefinition-allowedUnits extension now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack rather than active core source.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current build-scope source already implements the requested reference and the linked terminology page now explains the Quantity binding semantics.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Questionnaire issue clarifying that unitOption/unitValueSet constrain quantity-answer units as required-style lists; it is extension-specific and not a separate FHIR-13353 datatype-page change.
